title: Understanding the Difference Between Private Travel and Commercial Driving: A Constitutional Right Revisited
summary: Substack essay arguing private travel is a constitutional right free of licensing, registration and insurance, citing right-to-travel and licence-tax cases.

assertions.quote: a constitutionally protected right to travel in their private automobiles—free from the burden of licensing, registration, or insurance
The legal term "driver" denotes someone who is engaged in the transportation of goods or passengers for hire, compensation, or profit.
the right to travel by automobile is part of the liberty ... this right does not depend on the possession of a driver’s license
would be an unconstitutional conversion of a right into a taxable or regulated privilege

verdicts.note: Murdock concerned religious speech; courts hold driving on public roads is subject to licensing and fees.

The Supreme Court upheld registration and operator license fees graduated by horsepower as a valid police-power measure and fair compensation for roads, not a violation of the right to pass through the state.

assertions.quote: This decision affirmed that the constitutional right to travel is fundamental
